about.title: Redding Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Seven people did not come home from Redding's roads in 2025, according to public collision records for the year. Behind each of those numbers is a household in Shasta County now sorting through funeral arrangements, unpaid bills, and a silence no one prepared for. When a death follows someone else's careless driving on Churn Creek Road, Route 273, Hilltop Drive or Hartnell Avenue — or a preventable failure somewhere else entirely — California law gives certain family members a civil path to hold that party accountable. A wrongful death claim is not a criminal case; it moves on its own track, whether or not prosecutors ever file charges. It can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Redding families with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency, so you can ask questions without adding another expense to an already difficult season.

whyChoose.title: Why Redding Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who is allowed to file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An independent attorney can confirm where your family fits before anyone spends time on paperwork.

items.title: Deadlines tracked from day one
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Getting connected early keeps those dates from slipping past while you grieve.

items.title: A full accounting of what was lost
items.desc: Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial costs to the financial support your loved one provided and the love, companionship and guidance that no longer fill the house. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The crash that killed my family member happened on Route 273 in Redding. Does the road matter to the claim?
items.answer: It can. Route 273 is a state highway, and if a claim involves a public agency — for road conditions, a government vehicle, or a city or county employee — California requires a formal claim to that agency on a much shorter timeline than the usual two years. An attorney can look at the collision report and tell you whether any government involvement changes your deadlines.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges in Shasta County. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action, and it does not depend on a conviction or even on charges being filed. The two cases can move at the same time, and evidence gathered in the criminal matter is sometimes useful in the civil one. Waiting for the criminal case to wrap up can put your two-year deadline at risk.

items.question: We were not married, but we lived together for years. Can I bring a claim?
items.answer: Registered domestic partners have the same standing as spouses under California law, and children of the deceased come first alongside them. If you were not registered, standing may depend on whether you can show financial dependence on the person who died. This is exactly the kind of question worth putting to an independent attorney early, and LawProactive can make that connection for free.
